name: Glass jars
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register expressed in the food-contact FOOD basis (the register's other migration instruments — the EU 2009/48 toy Categories I to III and the ASTM F963 soluble limits — are in the toy article-extraction basis and are barred from every row of this category). Rows whose principal food-contact surface is a polymer anchor it directly, or by disclosed read-across where the instrument's own scope article excludes or does not reach the material or where the taxonomy row also carries a non-plastic configuration. Metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows, and the two water-treatment-device rows, are controls because their dedicated release regimes (Directive 84/500/EEC as amended by 2005/31/EC, the metals-and-alloys release regime, and the drinking-water device route) are not in the register in their own jurisdictions' rows. Where one taxonomy row carries both a polymer and a metal configuration, the published cells take the metal-article control and the plastics value is disclosed as a film-only companion.
native_basis: element release from the glaze, vitreous enamel or glass into food or food simulant, declared in TWO native bases: ug/dm2 of food-contact surface for non-fillable and shallow articles and for decoration within 20 mm of the lip (Directive 84/500/EEC Category I convention), and ug/L of 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid extract for fillable articles (Category II) and for articles over three litres and cooking ware (Category III), reportable as ug/kg only on the explicitly stated 1 L = 1 kg convention
native_basis_label: element RELEASE FROM THE GLAZE, VITREOUS ENAMEL OR GLASS NETWORK INTO FOOD OR A FOOD SIMULANT, declared in TWO NATIVE BASES because the governing release regime is written in two and this row never merges them. BASIS A, for non-fillable and shallow articles and for any decoration lying within 20 mm of the lip: ug per dm2 of food-contact surface, the Directive 84/500/EEC Category I convention. BASIS B, for fillable articles (Category II) and for articles over three litres and cooking ware (Category III): ug per litre of 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid extract, reportable as ug/kg ONLY on the explicitly stated 1 L = 1 kg convention, which is the single unit conversion this row permits. CONVERSION OF A PER-AREA RESULT INTO A PER-MASS OR PER-VOLUME RESULT IS FORBIDDEN on this row: it requires a food-contact-area-per-kg-of-food assumption (the occurrence literature commonly uses 5 dm2 per kg of foodstuff) that this standard does not adopt, and adopting it would smuggle an unstated assumption into a certification number. Every result is reported in the basis its article form generates, and a per-dm2 result and a per-litre result are never pooled, averaged or compared. This is a RELEASE basis and not a total-content basis, and it is deliberately NOT the Reg (EU) 10/2011 plastics-simulant convention: a plastics specific migration limit is never substituted for a release limit on this family.
scope_note: The glass container as filled, together with its closure system. The principal food-contact material is the glass network, whose element release regime is not present in the register as rows of its own jurisdiction; the only register rows carrying release numbers for this article family are four non-allowlisted Uruguayan rows, named and declined on stated grounds in every cell. The row is a control. The closure's plasticised sealing compound is a plastic gasket in a cap or closure and is directly within Reg (EU) 10/2011 Art. 2(1)(d), so that component is bound by the plastics migration ceilings as a companion obligation reported under the caps-and-closures row; the metal closure shell falls to the metal-article release control regime. TRACEABILITY OF THE COMPONENT POINTER: where this row's component plan refers a plastic component to "the plastics migration ceilings", that phrase resolves to a concrete published set of values inside this same standard and is not an unresolved pointer. It means the Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II values published on this category's plastics rows — eu_10_2011_pb_sml_nd (lead, not detectable at 10 ug/kg food), eu_10_2011_cd_sml_nd (cadmium, 2), eu_10_2011_tas_sml_nd (total arsenic, 10), eu_10_2011_thg_sml_nd (total mercury, 10), eu_10_2011_ni_sml (nickel, 20), eu_10_2011_al_sml (aluminium, 1000) and eu_10_2011_crtotal_sml_nd (total chromium, not detectable at 10), with tin excepted because the instrument lists no tin entry. Those values bind the plastic component as a SEPARATE obligation in its own material family and are never this row's published ceiling, which stays in this row's own native basis.
material: Soda-lime-silica container glass body; metal (tinplate or aluminium) twist or lug closure with a plasticised sealing compound; occasional applied ceramic labelling or exterior decoration.
components: Sample and report separately: (1) interior glass surface, filled-article extraction; (2) plasticised sealing compound of the closure, migration test against the actual food or the appropriate simulant; (3) interior surface of the metal closure shell, including any lacquer and any exposed cut edge; (4) applied ceramic labelling or exterior decoration where it lies within 20 mm of the sealing surface or the lip.
basis_guard: element release|specific release|release into food|release into a food simulant|release into the food simulant|acetic acid|food-contact surface area|mg/dm2|per dm2
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as element RELEASE from a glaze, vitreous-enamel or glass food-contact surface into food, a food simulant or the 4 percent (v/v) acetic acid extract convention, per dm2 of food-contact surface or per litre of extract, may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap. DECLARED VACUOUS STATE (recorded, not overlooked): as written this guard matches ZERO live, non-draft and non-quarantined rows in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and that is its intended state. The release regime this row's basis family belongs to is not in the register in any form this row may bind, which is the same fact this row's control cells record and state in detail; a guard that admitted a live row today could only do so by admitting a foreign basis. The guard is nevertheless expressed in the register's own basis vocabulary (element or specific release, release into food or a food simulant, 4 percent acetic acid extract, per dm2 of food-contact surface, net device contribution to the treated water) so that a future correct ingest of that regime BINDS through it. The previous prose-sentence guard on this row would have REJECTED the very instruments it was waiting for and forced them to a gap, which is the defect this rewrite removes. Two limits on the guard's force are stated plainly rather than left implicit: the compiler returns on the control branch before basis resolution, so a guard is never evaluated on a control cell, and this note rather than the machine is what carries the guard's force on this row today. The engine change that would close that hole - an assertion that every declared basis_guard either matches at least one live register row or carries basis_guard_vacuous_by_design, failing the build otherwise - is recorded as a tooling gap and is outside this config's scope.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.
